style.vernacular: A Soviet-planned city of limestone and render: low pre-war pastel-rendered houses and 19th-century Russian-era limestone buildings in the centre, Stalinist neoclassical blocks with columns along Stefan cel Mare, then rings of grey 5 to 9-storey prefabricated panel apartment blocks with balconies, and newer glass-and-cladding offices and malls after 1991. Orthodox churches have green or blue domes. Flat bitumen roofs on blocks, hip roofs in grey metal or red-brown tile on houses; poplar, linden, chestnut, acacia and willow trees.
style.ornament: Stalinist neoclassical columns, pediments and cornices on civic buildings; Soviet relief panels and mosaics on panel blocks; Corinthian-capital arches and denticulated cornices on 19th-century Russian-era classical buildings; Orthodox onion or flattened domes in green and blue metal; Moldavian geometric carpet motifs; local Cricova limestone walls.

sources.what: old Soviet-style apartment-block clusters are a large part of the city; much of the city built from limestone quarried at Cricova; post-1991 office and shopping complexes; 19th-century Orthodox churches
1841 Russian-era classical white-stone arch with ceramic Corinthian capitals
1807-1810 classicist church decoration: denticulated cornice, frieze, decorative frames
Stalinist-style rebuild of the station after 1941/1944 bombing
